subject: Helix pilot — Data handling confirmation (no training; residency & logs)
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Thompson <avery@horizonhealth.co>, Legal Ops <legal-ops@horizonhealth.co>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Helix pilot — Data handling confirmation (no training; residency & logs)

Hi Avery / Legal team —

Thanks again for taking the pilot demo earlier. Per our call, wanted to capture the data-handling commitments we discussed so your security and procurement folks can sign off quickly. Please confirm any corrections, otherwise we'll include these points in the DPA and pilot SOW.

Key items we agreed on the call:
- No model training on customer data: Redwood will not use Horizon Health production data to continue or improve models (no tuning, no fine-tuning, no dataset ingestion).
- Logging and PII: runtime logs will be captured for debugging but PII will be redacted at the SDK edge where possible; any tokens that may contain PHI/PII will be hashed/masked per your guidance.
- Retention: pilot logs retained 30 days by default; extended retention requires written agreement.
- Residency: model inference and log storage will operate in the us-west (Oregon) region for this pilot; if you require EU residency we can discuss Dedicated/Private options.
- Audit evidence: we can provide scoped SOC 2 evidence and a logging snapshot for the pilot window.

Next steps we proposed:
1) Legal to confirm opt-out of training and accept retention window (30 days) or propose alternate.
2) Redwood to add the training opt-out clause to the DPA draft and mark required security controls. (Attached: Helix_DPA_draft.pdf)
3) Technical kickoff scheduled once DPA terms are agreed.

If you confirm in a reply, we will treat that as binding for the pilot setup and update the contract.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: Helix_DPA_draft.pdf (PDF, 98KB)

Subject: Re: Helix pilot — Data handling confirmation (no training; residency & logs)

Hi Jasmine —

Thanks for the recap. Horizon Legal confirms high level acceptance of the opt-out from training on customer data. A few clarifying points: 

- We need explicit language in the DPA stating "Redwood will not use Customer Content for model development, training, or benchmarking outside of the scope of the agreed pilot."
- For logging: we require that any retained logs that could contain PHI are stored encrypted at rest, access-controlled, and that Redwood documents the redaction approach. Please confirm whether redaction happens client-side (recommended) or in Redwood's pipeline.
- Retention: 30 days is acceptable for the pilot, provided we can request an export prior to deletion. Please confirm the export format and access window.
- Residency: Pilot must store logs in us-west for now. If the pilot expands beyond 3 months we will re-evaluate EU residency requirements.

We reviewed the attached DPA draft — Legal will provide a redline with the training opt-out clause and a short amendment for the retention/export commitment by EOD tomorrow.

Regards,
Lydia Harper
Senior Counsel, Horizon Health — Legal Ops
legal-ops@horizonhealth.co

Lydia —

Appreciate the quick review and the requested language. To confirm Redwood's operational commitments for the pilot: 

- Training opt-out clause: we'll add the exact phrasing Lydia suggested into a DPA amendment (we'll send a redline). That clause will be explicit and irrevocable for the pilot dataset.
- Redaction approach: our standard for pilots is SDK-edge redaction/masking for well-known PII fields (SSN, full DOB, medical identifiers). For unstructured text, we apply a configurable redaction heuristic server-side and persist only masked tokens. We will provide a short technical note describing the heuristics and a sample log export schema.
- Export: we can produce a JSONL export of logs for the pilot window on request; Horizon will have 72 hours to retrieve an export prior to scheduled deletion. Exports will be encrypted in transit.
- Storage & access: pilot logs will be encrypted at rest, stored in us-west, and access will be scoped to the pilot engineering and support team. Any audit/demo requests will be coordinated and logged.

Next steps (internal): Monica — can you take point on creating the export template and updating the DPA redline with the technical bullet points? Jasmine — once we get Legal's redline, I'll approve and we ship the amendment.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

This aligns with what we discussed — Horizon confirms the following and consider this sufficient for pilot signoff:
